newsitem.title: NORWAY: Christiania to cut staff by nine percent.
newsitem.headline: Christiania to cut staff by nine percent.

text.p: Norway's second largest commercial bank, Christiania Bank og Kreditkasse ASA, announced on Tuesday it plans to reduce staff by nine percent, or 390 people, in the next two years.

Christiania officials, in interviews with Norwegian radio and the national news agency NTB, said new computer technology now being introduced, such as telephone banking, was making some jobs redundant.

The cuts, agreed at a Christiania board meeting on Monday, will be carried out through attrition and offers of early retirement through 1997 and 1998. About 230 million crowns ($35.7 million) earmarked for severance and other payments linked to the reductions will burden the 1996 accounts, the officials said.
The slimming down of operations will lead to an annual cost reduction of an estimated 130 million crowns, they said.
More job cuts may follow after 1998, a spokesman told NTB.

Several other banks and insurance companies, including Den norske Bank ASA (DnB) and Storebrand ASA, announced personnel cuts in 1996 to streamline operations and meet shrinking profit margins in Norway's overbanked financial sector. ($ = 6.446 Norwegian Crowns)
